title: Writing on tour with a pump organ
summary: He worked in hotel rooms with a small pump organ, still learning arranging by hearing the chords.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Let's see, we got to Chicago and -- oh, we got to Indianapolis, and there we ran into Hoagy. In the Whiteman band, they had a little hand organ and Whiteman had the manager, the guy who handled all the instruments, the baggage man besides -- he wasn't exactly a baggage man, but that was his job on the
road, he took care of the music, he took care of everything. He would bring it up to my room in the hotel, and I would have something to work on.
Was that a little pump organ.
Yeah, you pumped it with your feet and I didn't like using it much, but I was the kind of the guy that had to -- I had to hear what I was doing. A lot of guys -- see, I'm not studying or anything.
I know. You're still learning on the road.
I'm still lapping things up. So what was important to me was to hear what I had done and to hear the chords and I got a lot of instruments to fill in the chorus, to fill in the parts.

So I am sure I am not doing it in a very orthodox way. I am just taking this section and making that sound and this section and making that sound and I am doing a lot of it on paper but at the same time I still had it here.
